summary:
NOT acceptable yet — one major hole in D18 is still open, and I reproduced it myself.

D18 says that while a theory is being interpreted, nothing may hand the agent a stored English interpretation of that theory's own entities. The shipped fix closes the two lookup tools (`query`, `desugar_and_explain`). It does not close a third path nobody looked at: the batch prompt itself. When a theory declares a locale and also interprets it (`interpretation` / `sublocale` / `global_interpretation` in the same file — 1955 AFP theory files declare a locale and carry such a command), each generated fact carries a provenance hint composed on the Isabelle/ML side, and that hint embeds the STORED interpretation of the instantiated locale and of the template theorem. My probe with the production classes prints, inside `build_prompt`:
    Locale "T.L": OLD STORED TEXT OF THE LOCALE
    Template meaning: OLD STORED TEXT OF THE TEMPLATE
for exactly the key that `mk_query_by_name_tool(conn, hidden_keys=task.theory_keys)` refuses. A locale is one of the four gate-tracked kinds, so this is the flow-INT-1 failure verbatim: the agent is asked to re-interpret L while being shown L's previous text; an echo makes the judge say "same", `_write` then stores the NEW digest with the OLD version, `_propagate` never runs, and the whole downstream cone stays stale with no later scan re-listing it. The fix belongs where the text is formed (`build_entries` in Tools/semantic_store.ML), so that the payload a run sends can carry no stored text of that run's own entries by construction.

Everything else the integration judge ordered is correct as shipped. I re-checked each: `update_gate_fields` binds, checks and writes one dict (storage-S2); the lock acquire converts `Remote_Calling_Failure` inside the `\<^try>` body so the finaliser still closes the connection (ml-ML-INT-1); `_stop_if_cancelled` raises a fresh CancelledError and the laundering test fails when I revert it; `_label` / the answer-schema enum are output-identical (elegance-INT-2); the desugar branch hides before the query and before `seen_constants.add`; hover.py touches no stored interpretation at all.

Two real gaps beyond the hint, both cheap. (1) D19's live half is entirely unpinned: I ran the suite with `_statement` reverted to the bare wire text ONLY for `_write`'s call and got 403 passed / the same 16 pre-existing failures — byte-identical to the baseline. The one empty-wire `_write` call in the whole suite has `rec is None`, where both rules agree. I wrote and ran the five-line live-path test: it passes on the shipped code and fails `assert '' == 'nat'` under that mutation. (2) The interpretation system prompt still states the pre-D18 rule ("you cannot query entries you have been asked to translate"), contradicting the tool text the same change rewrote; the agent keeps the system prompt longest and will burn a tool call plus an error turn per sibling constant before learning the real rule.

The rest are small consistency repairs: `_prefilter` still renders both judge documents under the raw wire statement while its own docstring claims "the entity's current statement ... by the ONE document-text authority"; one comment still says the gate writes `expr = e.prop_str`; the notation fallback now carries a third copy of the same three-line prefix; and seven plan sentences still describe deleted machinery (`enrolled_names`, `_GATE_FIELDS`, the pre-D19 refresh guard).

Re-review after the ML hunk lands (pytest cannot exercise it); the rest can be checked by reading.

rulings.title: The batch prompt hands the agent the stored interpretation of this theory's locale and template theorem
rulings.rationale: CONFIRMED by my own probe, and it is the exact failure D18 exists to close. Chain, each link read on disk: Tools/semantic_store.ML:844-858 `sem_of` returns `query_semantics_by_key uk false` (the RPC that reads the stored record) for any key the store `contains` — `available` (:805-822) is only 'the store has this key', nothing excludes the run's own entries; :882-884 wraps those texts as `Template meaning: …` and `Locale "…": …`; :891-893 puts both into `hint`; the hint rides the wire (:1796-1820) into `Entry.prompt_extra` (semantic_interpretation.py:1956) and `format_entries` prints prompt_extra verbatim into the batch prompt, the retry prompt and the answer tool's reply (:770-773). `_collapse_provenance` (:740-760) drops the locale line only when it repeats the PREVIOUS entry's, so the first occurrence always prints. The key is the same one the guard refuses: mk_instance_hint's `luk` = `#1 (Universal_Key.key_of_locale context (#locale_name p))` (semantic_store.ML:794) and a locale entry's key = `Universal_Key.key_of NONE context (Locale name)` = `#1 (key_of_locale context name)` (Isabelle_RPC/Tools/Universal_Key.ML:986); locales declared in this theory ARE entries (theory_structure.ML:90-104 excludes only parents), so their keys are in `theory_keys` (semantic_interpretation.py:482). My probe built an InterpretationTask over a locale entry T.L plus a sibling fact carrying the hint mk_instance_hint composes; `build_prompt` printed both `Locale "T.L": OLD STORED TEXT OF THE LOCALE` and `Template meaning: OLD STORED TEXT OF THE TEMPLATE`. Reachability is not exotic: 1955 theory files in contrib/afp-2026-05-13/thys both declare a locale and carry an `interpretation`/`sublocale`/`global_interpretation` command. Failure: theory T declares `locale L … begin lemma foo … end` and interprets it as `q`; L's body changes, so L is a seed and the regenerated `q.foo` is a fresh uncached entry in the same session; the agent re-interprets L with L's old English text in front of it; an echo gives UNCHANGED, `_write` (:1387-1394) stores the new digest with the old version and baseline, `_propagate` does not run (`if minted`), and the cone below L is permanently stale. Severity blocker: it defeats D2/D18 silently and permanently, and it is the very defect the previous round ruled fix-then-rereview. Re-review is needed because the fix is Isabelle/ML, which pytest cannot exercise.
rulings.fix:
Close it where the text is composed, so nothing downstream has to remember. In `build_entries` (Tools/semantic_store.ML), seed a table with this batch's own keys and drop them before the `contains` call — the file already uses this idiom at :1300:

    (* D18: no stored interpretation of an entry of THIS run reaches the agent.
       The hint degrades to head + Template line — its shape when the store holds
       no text — and the agent reads the locale from the source. *)
    val own_uks : unit Bytehashtab.table = Bytehashtab.empty (Int.max (16, length raw))
    val _ = List.app (fn (_, _, _, uk) => Bytehashtab.update own_uks (uk, ())) raw
    val wanted_uks =
      prim_provenance |> maps (fn NONE => [] | SOME (t, l, _) => map_filter I [t, l])
      |> distinct (op =)
      |> filter_out (Bytehashtab.defined own_uks)

`available` then never holds such a key, `sem_of` returns NONE, and the RPC round trip for keys that would be discarded disappears as well. A locale imported from a parent theory is not in `raw`, so the hint keeps working unchanged in the common case. Do NOT fix this on the Python side: `Entry.locale_provenance` does carry template_uk/locale_uk, but stripping there means re-parsing prose the ML side composed. Then update the plan (edits 1 and 2 below).

rulings.title: D19's gate-write half is unpinned
rulings.rationale: CONFIRMED, and I reproduced both halves of the evidence. Suite baseline: 403 passed, 16 pre-existing failures. With a pytest plugin that makes `_statement` return the bare wire text ONLY when its caller is `_write`: 403 passed, the same 16 — byte-identical. A recorder plugin over the four gate/driver test modules shows every empty-wire `_statement` call: `[('_write', 'T.coll', None), ('_refresh_statements', 'a', 'nat')]` — the single `_write` call has `rec is None` (a first write), where the pre-D19 and post-D19 rules agree, so nothing exercises the rule. `test_an_empty_wire_statement_keeps_the_stored_one` (test_incremental_criteria.py:162-174) drives the DRY path, i.e. `_refresh_statements`, whose behaviour D19 did not change (the old truthiness guard already skipped the empty case). So the live write — the only behaviour D19 alters, and the one that can blank a stored statement and tombstone its vector — has no test. Same substance as agreement-tests-D19-WRITE; both are fixed by the one test below. Severity minor, matching the integration judge's own precedent on tests-F1, the mirror gap.
rulings.fix:
Add the live-path test beside the gate tests (test_semantic_change_gate.py). I ran this body myself: it passes on the shipped code and fails `assert '' == 'nat'` under the `_write`-only mutation.

    def test_an_empty_wire_statement_keeps_the_stored_expr_on_the_gate_s_write(run):
        _store("a", "the a", DG["a"])                 # stored expr "nat"
        entries = [_entry("a", DG2["a"], prop="")]    # the statement could not be computed
        run.go([_answer_batch()], entries, verdicts={"T.a": False})
        r = _rec("a")
        assert (r.interpretation, r.version) == ("new a", 2), "the gate did write"
        assert r.expr == "nat", "D19: the stored statement stands"

rulings.title: Reverting `_write` to `expr=e.prop_str` leaves the whole suite green
rulings.rationale: Same finding as d18-D19-4, with the mutation and the test body spelled out; I reproduced both (403 passed / 16 failed under the `_write`-only mutation, identical to baseline; the proposed test passes on the shipped code and fails under it). The analysis of why `_refresh_statements` is behaviour-identical to the pre-D19 guard is correct: the old `if e.prop_str and rec.expr != e.prop_str` skipped the empty case by truthiness, and the new `expr = _statement(e, rec); if rec.expr != expr` skips it because `expr` IS `rec.expr`. One fix covers both ids; also extend §10's D19 bullet (plan edit 9).
rulings.fix: As in d18-D19-4: add `test_an_empty_wire_statement_keeps_the_stored_expr_on_the_gate_s_write` to test_semantic_change_gate.py, and extend the §10 D19 bullet (plan:746-747) from "(dry path: byte-identical record)" to "(dry path: byte-identical record; live path: the gate's write keeps the stored `expr`)".

rulings.title: The interpretation system prompt still states the pre-D18 rule
rulings.rationale: CONFIRMED and in scope. semantic_interpretation.py:245 says "However, you cannot query entries you have been asked to translate — do it yourself.", which asserts that everything else IS queryable; semantics.py:1749-1751 now says "Entities of the theory you are interpreting cannot be queried — read their definitions from the source file yourself." The pre-D18 pair was consistent (the old tool text at semantics.py read "Do not query entries you have been asked to interpret"), so D18 introduced the contradiction by rewriting one of the two texts. `_SYSTEM_PROMPT` is used at :1851, the interpretation session, exactly where `hidden_keys=task.theory_keys` is passed at :1840, so the contradiction is live on every run; and by its own comment (:196-200) the system prompt is re-sent verbatim on every request and is never compacted away, so the WRONG text is the one the agent keeps longest. Concrete cost: the agent believes it may look up a same-theory dependency it was not assigned, and pays a tool call plus an `is_error` turn per such constant before it learns otherwise. This is an agent-facing text, not a §12 user-visible text, so it is not owed to step 8 — the other agent-facing texts were changed with D18.
rulings.fix: Rewrite semantic_interpretation.py:245 in the tool's own words, e.g.: "However, you cannot query ANY entity of the theory you are interpreting — read its definition from the source file yourself; entities of other theories you may query freely."

rulings.title: `_prefilter` renders both judge documents under the raw wire statement, not under D19's statement
rulings.rationale: CONFIRMED as a self-contradiction, not as a wrong verdict. semantic_interpretation.py:1304 builds both documents from `e.prop_str`, while the docstring three lines above (:1292-1294) says the two texts are rendered "each under the entity's current statement ... by the ONE document-text authority" — and since D19 the entity's current statement is `_statement(e, rec)` (:1238), which is what `_write` stores at :1387 and what `_refresh_statements` compares at :1251. So for an entity whose wire statement is empty (reachable: Tools/semantic_store.ML:720-723 `handle TYPE _ => "" | ERROR _ => ""` for a constant's constraint lookup, :724-727 `source_at_pos` returning "" for a type/class/locale), the pair the §7 threshold is applied to is not the pair the record will have. I checked the direction of the effect: the prefilter only short-circuits to CHANGED (`if sim is not None and sim < _GATE_SIMILARITY`), so restoring the shared statement prefix raises the cosine and merely sends more entities to the judge — no verdict can flip to UNCHANGED behind the judge's back. Hence minor, and an elegance/consistency defect rather than a correctness one: three places render "the entity under its statement" and only two follow the one rule D19 created. `_gate` holds `rec` at :1443 and `_prefilter` is only ever called at :1446 under `rec is not None`, so the fix is a parameter.
rulings.fix: Pass the statement down: `_prefilter(task, e, rec.baseline_interpretation, text, statement=_statement(e, rec))` at :1446 and build the docs with it at :1304, so the fresh document is byte-identical to the document of the record `_write` is about to store. If the user would rather not touch the prefilter at all, then the docstring at :1292-1294 must stop claiming "the entity's current statement" and say "under the wire statement" — one of the two has to change.

rulings.title: The 'do not let `_judge` absorb a teardown' invariant is enforced arm by arm, and one arm skips it
rulings.rationale: CONFIRMED as a structural weakness, and the challenger was honest that it is not reachable today — I agree, and I checked: `FatalAgentError` is raised only for deterministic driver conditions or by `_retry_unanswered`:1509 after completed turns, and no driver mentions CancelledError at all (and `except Exception` could not catch it anyway, since CancelledError is a BaseException). The structural point stands and the project rule is explicit that a shape making an invariant impossible to violate beats one asking people to remember it. `_stop_if_cancelled` now carries two jobs: (i) do not recycle a session the group is tearing down — a property of `_run_agent`'s recovering arms, correctly placed at :1585, :1589, :1597, :1611; (ii) do not hand `_judge`'s `except Exception` (:1335) an ordinary exception, because it reads any session failure as CHANGED and the gate then writes and mints on a torn-down run. Job (ii) is a property of the `_judge`/`_run_agent` boundary but is implemented as four calls on the other side of it, and the fifth arm — `except FatalAgentError:` … `raise` at :1598-1605 — re-raises precisely the class `_judge`'s own docstring names as reading CHANGED. Moving job (ii) to the boundary is a three-token change that costs nothing: the `finally` at :1339-1340 still adds the judge cost (it is synchronous), `_gate` still never reaches `_write`, and the misleading "verdict CHANGED" warning is skipped on a teardown.
rulings.fix: Make `_judge`'s handler `except Exception: _stop_if_cancelled(); _log.warning(...)` (semantic_interpretation.py:1335). Leave `_run_agent`'s four calls exactly as they are — they keep their own job (i) — and reword `_stop_if_cancelled`'s docstring: first paragraph 'called first in every recovering arm of `_run_agent`: a recycled session would be refused by the tearing-down group'; second paragraph 'and first in `_judge`'s `except Exception`, which reads any session failure as CHANGED and would otherwise let the gate write and mint on a run being torn down'.

rulings.title: The notation fallback's hidden branch drops show_defs and is a third copy of the same three-line prefix
rulings.rationale: PART REJECTED, part upheld. Rejected: the claim that the hidden branch should still honour `show_defs`. The tool's main path does exactly the same thing — semantics.py:1789-1791 returns `refused(typed)` before ever reaching `_append_definition` — so a refusal that omits the defining command is the shipped shape of the refusal, not a slip at this one branch; re-deciding how helpful a refusal should be is a design question for the user, and if it is ever re-opened it must move all refusal sites together, not one. Upheld: the duplication. semantics.py:1710-1715, :1723-1726 and :1727-1732 now each build the same three lines ('"x" is a notation (syntax: …)', 'It desugars to: …', 'Underlying constant: …') and differ only in the tail; D18 added the third copy, so a change to the notation report now has to be made in three places inside one function. That is a genuine, verified inelegance in code this change touched, and the repair is behaviour-preserving.
rulings.fix:
In `_try_resolve_syntax_token`, bind the prefix once and choose only the tail, keeping today's behaviour exactly:

    prefix = (f'"{name}" is a notation (syntax: {display}).\n'
              f'It desugars to: {compact_str}\n'
              f'Underlying constant: {const_name}')
    if uk in hidden_keys:
        return prefix + '\n(It belongs to the theory being interpreted; read its definition from the source.)'
    sem = Semantic_DB.query(uk, with_pretty=with_pretty)
    result = prefix + (f'\n\n{sem}' if sem is not None else
                       f'\n(Not yet interpreted. Use `query` with name="{const_name}" '
                       f'or `desugar_and_explain` for more details.)')
    if show_defs: ...

Do not change which branches reach `_append_definition`.

rulings.title: The statement-refresh call site still justifies itself by the pre-D19 write rule
rulings.rationale: CONFIRMED, and it is not a 'please add a comment' request — it is a comment asserting an equation the code no longer satisfies, at the one place that explains why the live-path refresh cannot undo a gate write. semantic_interpretation.py:1922-1923 reads "every entry that left `_NOT_ENROLLED` was written by its gate with `expr = e.prop_str` and put back into rec_cache, so the guard is a no-op for it", while `_write` writes `expr=_statement(e, rec)` (:1387). I re-derived the conclusion and it does survive — `_statement(e, written_rec)` returns `written_rec.expr` in both the empty and the non-empty case — so this is a wrong reason under a right outcome, which is the kind that misleads the next reader into believing the gate stores the bare wire text. D19 rewrote the neighbouring docstrings (`_statement`, `_refresh_statements`) and §15.8 item 8 and missed this one. Duplicate of cancel-d19-stale-write-comment and of the code half of agreement-plan-D19-LEFTOVERS; one edit fixes all three.
rulings.fix: semantic_interpretation.py:1922-1923 — replace "was written by its gate with `expr = e.prop_str` and put back into rec_cache, so the guard is a no-op for it" with "was written by its gate with `expr = _statement(e, rec)` and put back into rec_cache, and `_statement` over that written record returns the same string, so the guard is a no-op for it".

rulings.title: Two comments still state that the gate writes `expr = e.prop_str`
rulings.rationale: Duplicate of d18-D19-5 for the :1920-1923 half, which I upheld there for the same reason (a false equation at the only site that justifies the refresh's no-op-ness). The second half — appending a D19 clause to `Entry.prop_str`'s field comment at :286 — I REJECT as a nitpick: 'printed proposition / type signature (Unicode); stored as expr' still states the rule, the exception has its own named function three lines from each of its two uses (`_statement`, :1233-1238), and padding a field comment with a per-case exception is exactly the comment bloat the project's 'comments are concise, load-bearing' rule exists to stop.
rulings.fix: Apply the :1922-1923 edit from d18-D19-5. Leave :286 alone.

rulings.title: §5.3.2 still prescribes the pre-D19 guard
rulings.rationale: CONFIRMED on the plan half, which is the substantive one: SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:317-319 reads "For every not-enrolled entry whose `prop_str` differs from the stored `expr` (today's guard verbatim, §15.8 item 8), `Semantic_DB.update_expr`". Read literally that prescribes the very blanking D19 forbids — an entry with `prop_str == ""` over a stored `expr` of "nat" does 'differ' — and "today's guard verbatim" is now false, because the code compares `_statement(e, rec)` (:1251). §15.8 item 8 (plan:1451-1457) was rewritten for D19 and correctly refers BACK to §5.3.2, so the plan now points from a correct section to a stale one. The code half (:1920-1923) is the same finding as d18-D19-5; one edit serves both.
rulings.fix: Plan edit 7 below, plus the :1922-1923 comment edit from d18-D19-5.

rulings.title: Three plan sentences still describe the deleted enrolment-keyed refusal, and neither class listing carries `theory_keys`
rulings.rationale: CONFIRMED, all four sites read on disk. plan:147 "(`mk_query_by_name_tool` refuses every enrolled name, §15.8)" — there is no name-keyed refusal left; the tool takes `hidden_keys` (semantics.py:1737-1743) and checks the RESOLVED key at :1789, :1803, :1710. plan:1057, inside §15.3's `InterpretationTask` listing, still declares `self.enrolled_names: list[str] = []   # appended by enqueue; shared with mk_query_by_name_tool` — deleted from the code, and it was never a field of `InterpretationTask` in the first place (it lived on `AgentTask`), so the plan declares a dead field on the wrong class. §15.2's `AgentTask.__init__` listing (plan:986-996) stops at `_progress` and never mentions `theory_keys`, although `__init__` sets it at semantic_interpretation.py:482 and D18 itself points at `AgentTask.theory_keys`. plan:1612 still describes the retargeted test by its old content. The plan is the authoritative design document; a deleted field still declared in it is a trap for the next implementer.

rulings.title: The plan's `__init__` sketch still declares the `enrolled_names` field D18 deleted
rulings.rationale: CONFIRMED, but it is a strict subset of agreement-plan-D18-LEFTOVERS and its section label is wrong: plan:1057 sits in §15.3 (`InterpretationTask`, heading at :1036), not in §15.8, and the line it quotes is the `InterpretationTask` listing — which makes the plan doubly wrong there, since the deleted field lived on `AgentTask`. The proposed replacement is also misplaced: `theory_keys` belongs in §15.2's `AgentTask` listing, where the code sets it (semantic_interpretation.py:482), not in §15.3's. Fixed by plan edits 4 and 5.
rulings.fix: Delete plan:1057 outright (§15.3's listing), and add the `theory_keys` line to §15.2's `AgentTask.__init__` listing instead — plan edits 5 and 4.

rulings.title: §10 still asks for a test on the `_GATE_FIELDS` set that storage-S2 deleted
rulings.rationale: CONFIRMED. plan:763 asks for "adding an embedded-doc field to the gate writer's set raises". There is no set: the diff deleted `_Semantic_DB._GATE_FIELDS` and the up-front `self._check_raw_put_grant("gate_write", self._GATE_FIELDS)`; `update_gate_fields` now binds `fields` and hands that same object to `_check_raw_put_grant` and to `_put_fields` (semantics.py:981-985). So the §10 bullet describes neither the code nor the retargeted test (test_semantic_change_gate_storage.py:214-235, which checks the helper directly and then pins the routing through a recorded `_check_raw_put_grant`). Small, but §10 is the plan's test contract and it now names a deleted constant.

rulings.title: D18's "every entity of that theory" over-claims under a `Context.Proof` root
rulings.rationale: CONFIRMED on the facts, and the challenger is right that no gate failure follows. Tools/theory_structure.ML:186-196: for a Proof context `parent_facts = [Global_Theory.facts_of (Proof_Context.theory_of ctxt)]`, so `Facts.dest_static false parent_facts facts` returns only proof-local facts and the theory's own global theorems are filtered out as 'parent'; constants/types/classes take the other route (:55-90, :168-180, kept when `#theory_long_name entry = thy_name`) and ARE enumerated. Proof roots are a real path: semantic_store.ML:2352 collects them and :2380-2386 runs `interpret'` on each, last and sequentially. So `theory_keys` = the run's enumerated entries, which under a Proof root is a proper subset of 'every entity of that theory'. The residue is harmless — a theorem-alike entry carries no digest (D15) and is never judged, and under a Proof root `provss` is `map (K []) raw` so no provenance hint is built either — which is why this is a wording defect, not a code defect. §15.8 already says the precise thing ("the universal keys of every entry of the theory"); it is only D18's row that is loose. I reject the proposed 60-word parenthetical as a cure worse than the disease; one word does it, and it folds into the D18 row rewrite that d18-D18-1 needs anyway.
rulings.fix: Folded into plan edit 1: say 'every entity this run enumerated for that theory' instead of 'every entity of that theory'. No separate edit, no code change.

plan_edits: §2, the D18 row (SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:102). CURRENT: "inside an interpretation session both lookup tools -- `query` and `desugar_and_explain` -- hide every entity of that theory, enrolled or not, keyed on the resolved universal key at every point a text would be returned (`AgentTask.theory_keys`, fixed at construction)."  PROPOSED: "inside an interpretation session nothing hands the agent a stored interpretation of an entity this run enumerated for that theory, enrolled or not, at any of the three points one could travel: both lookup tools -- `query` and `desugar_and_explain` -- refuse on the resolved universal key (`AgentTask.theory_keys`, fixed at construction), and on the ML side `build_entries` leaves such a text out of the locale-interpretation provenance hint it composes."  (The word 'enumerated' also settles the `Context.Proof` root, where the theory's global theorems are not entries and are not re-interpreted either.)

§15.8, the addressing paragraph (around :1458-1470), after "...and `mk_desugar_and_explain_tool`'s per-constant annotations (which say \"read its definition from the source\" instead)".  ADD: "The third point is upstream of Python: `build_entries` (semantic_store.ML) composes the locale-interpretation provenance hint, whose `Template meaning:` and `Locale \"...\":` lines carry stored interpretations. Those lines are omitted when the key is one of this run's own entries -- `wanted_uks` drops them before the `Semantic_Store.contains` call -- so the hint degrades to the shape it already has when the store holds no text, and no consumer of `Entry.prompt_extra` has to re-check anything."

§3, after the table (:147). CURRENT: "nothing consumed the superseded text (`mk_query_by_name_tool` refuses every enrolled name, §15.8)".  PROPOSED: "nothing consumed the superseded text (no stored interpretation of this theory's entities reaches the agent at all, D18/§15.8)".

§15.2, the `AgentTask.__init__` listing (:986-996), after the `self._progress = asyncio.Event()` line.  ADD: "        self.theory_keys: frozenset[bytes] = frozenset(e.universal_key for e in entries)   # D18: what the lookup tools hide".

§15.3, the `InterpretationTask` listing (:1057). CURRENT: "        self.enrolled_names: list[str] = []        # appended by enqueue; shared with mk_query_by_name_tool".  PROPOSED: delete the line (the field is gone from the code, and it was a field of `AgentTask`, never of `InterpretationTask`).

§15.10, the file mapping (:1612). CURRENT: "its mirror (after a CHANGED verdict enrols a dependent, `query` refuses that dependent's name; record byte-identical, no judge driver constructed, counter untouched)".  PROPOSED: "its mirror (D18: neither lookup tool discloses a stored interpretation of this theory's entities, enrolled or not, at the name lookup, the notation fallback, the short-name fallback or the desugar annotations, while an entity of another theory is served)".

§5.3.2 (:317-319). CURRENT: "For every not-enrolled entry whose `prop_str` differs from the stored `expr` (today's guard verbatim, §15.8 item 8), `Semantic_DB.update_expr` (invalidates vectors)."
